title: The Library That Grows Instead of Standing

features.name: root-shelf
features.desc-on-touch: you brush a shelf that emerges from dark loam, pages still damp with earth. the words here have not yet dried into fixed meaning.

features.name: reading-tree
features.desc-on-touch: a eucalyptus grows through the middle of this space, and you understand that its trunk is a spine—the books grew around it. you can open it to any page.

features.name: sprouted-catalogues
features.desc-on-touch: index cards are growing from gaps in the soil, each one alphabetizing something that has not yet been born. you can feel them organizing as you watch.

features.name: binding-vines
features.desc-on-touch: vines twist through the space, their tendrils stitching pages together. some bindings are fresh and supple. some are old as roots.

features.name: reading-light
features.desc-on-touch: a pale glow pools beneath one tree-hole, where mycorrhizal networks shine faintly. you can read by this light, which is the light of things learning to speak to each other.

reverie.title: REVERIE — sitting with the growing words
narr: you find her sitting among new-sprouted pages, root-bound,
and she's reading aloud to the soil. the words she speaks
sink down—they're teaching the earth to alphabetize itself.
leif is somewhere deeper, recording the sound of meaning
emerging. you sit beside her, and the binding-vines gently
catch your sleeve, asking: what do you want to grow here?

inscription: the literacy of the earth teaching itself the names of the things it was holding before anyone asked

file.name: RootAlphabet_PartialGlossary_Revised.txt
file.note: an index of words that grew instead of being catalogued, annotations in handwriting, some entries incomplete as if the writer were waiting for the forest to finish the thought

exits.label: back through the dark where literacy began
upward through branching that leads to light and reading rooms
deeper into loam, where the oldest unwritten words still sleep
